rules: Keep original benchmark text and benchmark code on each TextUnit.
Attach grade/course placement to the versioned TextUnit; do not bake grade into the scientific Concept.
Represent each proposed match as an EvidenceAssertion so several possible predecessors can coexist.
Conceptual alignment does not imply textual borrowing or authorship.
provenanceStatus records the evidence state for the drafting source; identified wording lineage does not identify an author, intermediary, or access path.
Use unresolved when matching evidence is insufficient; absence of a match is not proof of deletion.
An assessmentCrosswalk relation records an assessment/report alignment only; it does not assert one-to-one standard equivalence or source authorship.
A semanticNeighborCandidate is a machine-ranked discovery lead only; similarity scores do not establish borrowing, continuity, or omission and require human review.
A topicComparison records a reviewed content comparison; it does not establish that the source informed drafting or that text was copied.
An identifierMatch edge means only that normalized codes are shared; it does not imply wording or conceptual equivalence.
A normalized_exact_sentence_match edge means the benchmark sentence matches after Unicode NFKC and whitespace normalization; it does not identify an author or drafting source.
A containsBenchmark edge records code hierarchy parsed from the source document, not a conceptual relationship.
